newsitem.title: UK: Algeria hikes August crude price, Syrian undecided.
newsitem.headline: Algeria hikes August crude price, Syrian undecided.

text.p: Lifters of Algerian Saharan Blend crude agreed an August contract price of Dated Brent plus 52 to 53 cents with state oil company Sonatrach, traders said on Monday.
The August price is a 13 cents increase on July levels.
Lifters of Syrian crude were still waiting to hear from Sytrol, having requested that the oil company reconsider its original asking price of Dated Brent minus 40 cents for Syrian Light.
"We're still wait for a second response from Syria, we have asked them to reconsider the price," said one contract holder.
Buyers were originally seeking a rollover of July's discount of 55 cents to Dated Brent.
Sytrol was also seeking a contract price of Dated Brent minus $3.85 for its heavy Souedie grade, but buyers were hoping to pay less than Dated Brent minus $4.00.
The Urals market was quiet on Monday morning, in a lull between July and August sales. All July cargoes have found homes and traders were waiting for the August loading programme.
"No-one really knows much about August liftings, there is one cargo deferred from July to the next month," a trader said.
